scope: Woodford, Interest and Prices, Chapter 6: Inflation Stabilization and Welfare, with Appendix E. Second-order welfare approximations in two layers: exact polynomial identities with explicit terms independent of policy and explicit third-order remainders, and a one-parameter Taylor bridge from actual expected utility with O(eps^3) remainders and welfare-ranking corollaries. Approximation theory (1.2)-(1.10) corrected; Props 6.1-6.5 and the exact Calvo dispersion identities; Prop 6.6 with corrected weights; the case for price stability; transactions frictions and the zero lower bound with a proved two-constraint KKT theorem (Props 6.7-6.9); asymmetric disturbances and sticky wages (Props 6.10-6.13); cost-push shocks; large distortions with (5.1) corrected and the second-order AS (5.4) derived from the Calvo model (Props 6.14-6.15). Post-book: existence and uniqueness of a Markov equilibrium of the exact nonlinear Calvo model under a Taylor rule and under timeless Ramsey policy (finite trees and general filtered probability spaces, adapted, unique among all bounded processes, Markov in the state for AR(1) shocks with any bounded law, Prop 6.15 over a probability space of goods); smooth dependence of the policy on the shock scale sigma (C^k, certainty equivalence including regime switching, the sigma^2 correction, Props 6.7-6.15 along the perturbation equilibrium).
source: Michael Woodford, Interest and Prices: Foundations of a Theory of Monetary Policy, Princeton University Press, 2003, Chapter 6, pp. 381-463, and Appendix E, pp. 692-708.
